chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi and al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, all from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Tayyar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what requires zakat, and he said: 'In nine things: gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused what is other than that.'
I said: May Allah make you upright, for we have much grain (habb). He said: 'And what is it?' I said: Rice. He said: 'Yes, if it is abundant.'

I said: Is there zakat in it? He rebuked me, saying: 'I tell you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused what is other than that, and you say to me: We have much grain, is there zakat in it?'
ai.seo_question: What are the nine items subject to zakat in Shia jurisprudence, and how is rice treated?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the canonical nine categories (*al-athman al-tis'ah*) of zakatable assets, emphasizing the Prophet's general exemption of other goods unless they reach the abundance threshold of the primary grains. The dialogue regarding rice illustrates the Shia scholarly principle of *istihsan* (juristic preference) or analogical extension, where abundant staple foods are treated similarly to the explicitly mentioned wheat and barley. This reflects the practical application of prophetic tradition in determining fiscal obligations for agricultural produce in early Islamic society.
